## Before anyone opens the timeline

Fact-check flags from the script: (1) Check what discover-abilities actually lists before filming so 'apart from what WordPress and WooCommerce already expose' (sentence 102) is honest. (2) Confirm mcp-adapter.zip on the Releases page is still the latest release on the day (v0.6.1 at time of writing). (3) '${VAR}' expansion needs the variables set in the shell that launches Claude Code; the on-screen note in b26 covers this, keep it. (4) The Shop Manager order answers (b32) must visibly come through MCP tool calls, not a fallback route. (5) The SSH transcript (b36) must be the real one, on screen. (6) 'Being assessed for the plugin directory' (sentence 27) is hearsay unless you have a source; link one if you can. Plus from this edit: script cue 9 says 'then terminal' but v2 installs from the Releases zip, so the terminal is only needed for the optional build aside in b12. Script cue 20 asks for the finished file at sentence 61, before LOG_FILE is described in sentence 66, so the finished file is held in b26 instead. Sentence 98 says permissions can deny SSH commands outright; Wordmove runs ssh itself, so the on-screen deny list in b39 should cover wordmove, scp and rsync as well as ssh or the claim is weaker than it sounds. Check 'Claude Cowork' (sentence 112) is the product name you mean.

## Tone and style

Practical and personal, a British YouTuber talking to WordPress developers. Clean screen recordings at readable zoom (code at 1080p must be legible). Light, low music bed under the walkthroughs; drop it out for the SSH story (b35 to b40) and bring it back at b41. Captions on. Recurring graphics: numbered chapter cards for steps 1 to 5 in one style, and the kitchen illustration (hatch, jars, padlocks, key) built once and reused in b15 to b18, b33 and b37. On-screen text in British English, no em dashes. Zooms are simple punch-ins, not animated swoops.

**Blur list:** b05: new user's password field and email address; b08: the generated application password, for as long as it's on screen; b01 and b36: the SSH terminal transcript: hostnames, IP addresses, SSH usernames, ports, key paths, Movefile details; b32: customer names, addresses, phone numbers and emails in the order replies; b42: any customer names on booked slots in the CasaGees admin; b51: server hostname and username in the WP-CLI shell prompt; Anywhere: real values of WP_API_USERNAME and WP_API_PASSWORD if they ever appear (e.g. in a shell profile or env output)
